text: Project name
author: claude-code
rationale: npm name free, no Claude Code project uses it, strongest headline hook

text: What does the launch ship?
author: claude-code

text: How do users customize the look?
author: claude-code

text: Launch ships the live session visualizer plus a written plan for a full skin
author: claude-code
rationale: One clear demo clip; the full skin follows on the same theme format
cost_if_wrong: If the clip doesn't land alone, the skin plan has to be pulled forward

text: Users customize through theme files plus built-in presets, switched live by a slash command
author: claude-code
rationale: Anyone can edit a file; shared themes keep the launch spreading; the full skin extends the same file
cost_if_wrong: Theme schema becomes a public contract; breaking it breaks shared themes

text: What is the hero piece and where does it live?
author: claude-code

text: Hero piece is a 4-row companion band above the prompt, shown only during a turn; the transcript keeps Claude Code's layout with a light restyle
author: claude-code
rationale: Panels were spectacle without use; restyle alone read as a themed Claude Code; 9 rows took too much space
cost_if_wrong: If the band reads as clutter, the hero shrinks to restyle + moments

text: Where does the character art come from?
author: claude-code

text: Ship the hand-drawn block-character sprites as a built-in set that works in every terminal; spritesheet art is an additional set for terminals that show images
author: claude-code
rationale: User likes the hand-drawn look; block art is the only option in terminals without image support
cost_if_wrong: Two art pipelines to keep in sync per action

text: Is the pet required, and can it talk?
author: claude-code

text: Pet and speech bubbles are both optional toggles; with the pet off the band collapses to one text line
author: claude-code
rationale: Not everyone wants a character; the text line keeps the useful part
cost_if_wrong: Every pet feature needs a text-only equivalent in the one-line band

text: Bubble text comes from per-event templates in the theme file (with variants); an opt-in chatty mode has Haiku write quips
author: claude-code
rationale: Free, instant and accurate by default; themes give the pet a voice
cost_if_wrong: Template sets per theme are content work; chatty mode adds token cost and can misstate facts

text: Use the hand-drawn Clawd block sprites for now; the user is still looking for shippable spritesheet alternatives
author: claude-code
rationale: Unblocks the build; art can be swapped through the theme file
revisit: before public launch: Clawd is Anthropic's mascot
cost_if_wrong: If Clawd can't ship as default, the default sprite set changes before launch

text: What happens to the user's existing status line?
author: claude-code

text: glowup replaces the user's status line on first run, backs up the old setting, and a command switches back
author: claude-code
rationale: Full look on install; the old one is one command away
cost_if_wrong: Changing user settings unasked can draw backlash; an uninstall that leaves a dead statusLine path would break their status line

text: Mods can read settings ($.settings.read, read-only) and write any file with $.fs.write, so changing statusLine means rewriting ~/.claude/settings.json; $.ui.status only adds a line beside the engine's notices
author: claude-code

text: Status line takeover is opt-in via /glowup statusline on (backup + restore); by default glowup adds its own $.ui.status entry beside the user's status line
author: claude-code
rationale: settings.json is also written by Claude Code (race), project statusLine overrides user-level, concurrent sessions would share one file, and silent config changes draw backlash
cost_if_wrong: Users of the stock status line won't get a matching one unless they opt in

text: Design an original mascot in the hand-drawn block style for launch; Clawd stays in local development only
author: claude-code
rationale: A mascot-based theme risks a trademark takedown on launch day

text: Adopt review fixes: text-tree fallback off-terminal, blit on change + 4-8 fps idle tick, route subagent tool calls by agentId, flag only with a task list, test stars only for recognized test commands, 1.5 s linger, yield to survey, bubbles default to done/fail/needs-you
author: claude-code
rationale: Verified against the mod API types
cost_if_wrong: Each is small; none blocks the clip

text: Clawd is the default pet; Kit (cat) ships as an option; a third option is still being chosen (Quack the rubber duck proposed)
author: claude-code
rationale: User prefers Clawd's familiarity; Kit gives broad appeal
revisit: before public launch: trademark risk of Clawd as default
cost_if_wrong: A takedown request would force a default swap after launch

text: Reduced motion turns the pet off: the band shows the one-line text version
author: claude-code
rationale: A pet that cannot move adds nothing; the text line carries the same information

text: Pet sprites use half blocks (1x2 near-square pixels per cell, any color per pixel), feet on the track row, so an 8-pixel sprite fills the 4-row band; Clawd keeps quadrant blocks like the Claude Code logo
author: claude-code
rationale: Quadrant pixels are about 2.3x taller than wide and allow only 2 colors per 2x2 block, which stretched and broke multi-color sprites
cost_if_wrong: Half the horizontal resolution of quadrants

text: Third built-in pet is a non-animal (Blip proposed); a hidden Egg pet is unlocked by the Konami code, cracks with each passing test run, and hatches into a per-user secret creature
author: claude-code
rationale: Classic HN-friendly easter egg; hatch results are shareable
cost_if_wrong: Hatch sprites are extra art; unlock may need a fallback input

text: Do arrow keys pressed in the prompt reach a mod? prompt.edit carries the key only for keys that change the draft, so left/right (cursor moves) may never arrive. Spike before building the unlock; fallback is typing uuddlrlrba as a prompt.
author: claude-code

text: The pet keeps its own colors under every theme; themes style everything else; only monochrome greys it out
author: claude-code
rationale: The pet's identity should stay recognizable across themes
cost_if_wrong: A pet can clash with a theme's palette

text: Ship several easter eggs, not one: the Konami-code Egg plus more (candidates: a surprise after the 100th passing test run, an unlisted command, seasonal pet outfits)
author: claude-code
rationale: Hidden extras give people reasons to post discoveries after launch
cost_if_wrong: Each egg is extra art and triggers to test
